executive_summary: REQUIRE-X Multi-Agent AI Framework evaluated the Software Requirement Specification 'healthcare_srs.txt'. The specification comprises 16 total requirements (8 Functional, 8 Non-Functional) with an estimated agile effort of 73 story points. The document attained an ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 compliance score of 84.2% (Grade: B+). The framework generated 24 automated test cases, achieving 100.0% bidirectional traceability coverage mapped to a recommended Event-Driven Microservices Architecture blueprint.
key_strengths: Clear structural separation of 8 Functional Requirements across core system modules.
High traceability readiness (100.0% of requirements directly mapped to automated test suites).
Standardized numbering scheme compliant with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 standards.
key_risks: Identified 8 ambiguous or unquantified statements (50.0% defect rate) that introduce misinterpretation risks.
action_items: Review and approve the suggested disambiguated rewrites in the Ambiguity Audit tab.
Adopt the recommended Event-Driven Microservices Architecture component decomposition for architecture design.
Export the generated Requirement Traceability Matrix (RTM) and Test Suite into the project's QA management tool.

ambiguities.explanation: Statement is excessively brief and lacks input preconditions or expected measurable output state.
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The system shall payment amounts with specific input validation parameters and return status codes.

ambiguities.explanation: The term 'fast' is subjective and untestable without defined latency/response time thresholds (e.g., '< 200ms at 95th percentile').
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The system shall process patient search queries within 250 milliseconds under peak concurrent load of 1,000 requests/sec and return medical history with minimal delay.

ambiguities.explanation: Quantify allowable latency bounds in milliseconds.
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The system shall process patient search queries fast and return medical history with within a maximum threshold of 100 milliseconds.

ambiguities.explanation: 'Robust' is non-verifiable. Specify precise fault tolerance, error handling, or recovery MTTR bounds.
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The system shall be fault-tolerant with automated retry logic and 99.95% error-free transaction processing and handle high hospital data traffic as appropriate.

ambiguities.explanation: 'As appropriate' introduces implementation ambiguity. Specify exact operational conditions.
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The system shall be robust and handle high hospital data traffic upon detecting a validated user trigger event.

ambiguities.explanation: Passive construct 'be encrypted' obscures the system actor responsible for the action.
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The System shall explicitly execute the action rather than stating 'be encrypted'.

ambiguities.explanation: 'User-friendly' cannot be objectively verified. Define specific usability criteria, such as task completion rate > 90% or SUS score > 80.
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The user interface shall be conformant with WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines and enabling task completion in <= 3 user clicks, clean, and easy to use for medical staff on desktop tablets and workstation monitors.

ambiguities.explanation: 'Easy to use' lacks measurable criteria. Replace with maximum click depth or user training time bounds.
ambiguities.suggested_rewrite: The user interface shall be user-friendly, clean, and conformant with WCAG 2.1 AA guidelines and enabling task completion in <= 3 user clicks for medical staff on desktop tablets and workstation monitors.

compliance_scorecard.summary: The Software Requirement Specification achieved an overall ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 compliance score of 84.2% (B+). Identified 16 requirements (8 FR, 8 NFR) with 8 quality defects requiring disambiguation to ensure full contractual and verification readiness.

architecture.rationale: Selected Event-Driven Microservices architecture due to demanding non-functional requirements in Scalability, high throughput, and independent domain decoupling. Asynchronous messaging isolates failure domains and supports horizontal elastic autoscaling.
tradeoffs_pros: High horizontal scalability and fault isolation
Independent deployment lifecycles per domain service
tradeoffs_cons: Higher distributed tracing and operational complexity
Eventual consistency data management across services

components.name: API Gateway & Security Provider
components.responsibility: Handles TLS termination, routing, JWT token verification, rate limiting, and CORS.

components.name: Core Business Logic Engine
components.responsibility: Executes primary application workflows, business validation, and entity state transitions.

components.name: Data Management & Persistence Service
components.responsibility: Manages relational schemas, transaction integrity, indexing, and backup persistence.

components.name: Telemetry, Monitoring & Quality Guard
components.responsibility: Collects performance metrics, audit logs, error traces, and health status.

architecture.mermaid_diagram:
graph TD
    Client["Client Apps (Web / Mobile)"] --> Gateway["API Gateway (Auth & Rate Limit)"]
    Gateway --> ServiceA["Auth & Identity Service"]
    Gateway --> ServiceB["Core Business Engine Service"]
    Gateway --> ServiceC["Processing & Transaction Service"]
    Gateway --> ServiceD["Analytics & Reporting Service"]
    
    ServiceB <--> EventBus[("Event Bus (Kafka / RabbitMQ)")]
    ServiceC <--> EventBus
    ServiceD <--> EventBus
    
    ServiceA --> DB_Auth[("Auth Database")]
    ServiceB --> DB_Core[("Core DB (PostgreSQL)")]
    ServiceC --> DB_Trans[("Tx Store")]
    ServiceD --> DB_Analytics[("Analytics Warehouse")]
